extraction_text: Bhishma narrated an ancient dialogue between Indra and Nahusha.
Indra approached Nahusha, who had lost his wealth and position, and asked if he felt sorrow.

attributes.state: Nahusha was calm despite his losses

extraction_text: Nahusha explained that sorrow is destructive and should be controlled through contemplation of the highest good.

attributes.philosophy: Rejection of sorrow, emphasis on detachment and acceptance

extraction_text: Nahusha stated that there is only one supreme ruler (the divine/creator) who controls everything, including himself.

attributes.belief: Divine determinism, submission to a higher power

extraction_text: Nahusha emphasized that beings are reborn according to the creator's arrangement, not by their own will.

attributes.concept: Rebirth, fate, lack of control over circumstances

extraction_text: Nahusha noted that even sages, gods, and great asuras face disasters, but those who understand past and future remain unshaken.

attributes.observation: Universal suffering, wisdom as protection against distress

extraction_text: Nahusha described the ideal sage as unperturbed by success or failure, accepting all states equally.

attributes.ideal: Stoic equanimity, being a 'yoked one' (disciplined soul)

extraction_text: Nahusha concluded that since mortals cannot obtain the unobtainable through effort, sorrow is pointless, and one should accept the creator's design.

attributes.conclusion: Futility of sorrow, acceptance of fate, mastery over dualities
